sources.title: Llama Guard 3-8B Model Card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: explicitly identifies Llama Guard 3-8B as a Llama-3.1-8B pretrained model fine-tuned for content safety classification. The current card documents text safety labels, eight languages and 14 hazard categories; it gives no separate active count or structural-pruning claim for this standard 8B model.

sources.title: Meta Llama-Guard-3-8B repository metadata
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: exact repository revision remains 7327bd9f6efbbe6101dc6cc4736302b3cbb6e425, with explicit finetune:meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B metadata, LlamaForCausalLM architecture and BF16 safetensors element total 8,030,261,248. This metadata corroborates the existing derived learned-parameter total; no weight shards were downloaded.

sources.title: Meta model registry: exact Llama Guard 3 8B architecture
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: the standard Llama-Guard-3-8B entry targets meta-llama/Llama-Guard-3-8B and retains dimension 4096, 32 layers, 32 query heads, 8 KV heads, vocabulary 128256, FFN multiplier 1.3 and rounding multiple 1024. These count-defining dimensions match the Llama-3.1-8B base entry. A separate INT8 repository is registered; the standard model retains the full vocabulary.

sources.title: Meta Llama 3 reference Transformer implementation
sources.evidence: Defines bias-free attention and three-matrix gated FFN weights, two learned RMSNorm vectors per layer, separate vocabulary embedding/output matrices and final norm. Head dimension is dim/n_heads; FFN width is the rounded scaled two-thirds of 4*dim. RoPE frequencies and KV caches are computed non-parameter tensors.

sources.title: Meta model registry: context lengths and quantization defaults
sources.evidence: Explicitly returns max_seq_length 131072 for CoreModelId.llama_guard_3_8b. The unqualified model variant defaults to BF16; INT8 is distinct.

sources.title: Expanding our open source large language models responsibly
sources.evidence: Dated July 23, 2024; announces release of Llama Guard 3 as multilingual input/output moderation derived from Llama 3.1 and sharing of weights and safety tools.

sources.title: Llama Guard 3 model cards and prompt formats
sources.evidence: Distinguishes text-only 8B and 1B models from 11B-Vision, identifies 8B as released with Llama 3.1, and documents safety classification with S14 support in the 8B model.

sources.title: Current PurpleLlama Llama Guard 3 8B license copy
sources.evidence: Current GitHub directory contains Llama 3.2 Community License text, conflicting with the Llama 3.1 text and metadata in the exact Hugging Face weight repository. This discrepancy is recorded rather than silently transferring the newer license.

sources.title: The Llama 3 Herd of Models
sources.evidence: Section 3.2 describes dense Transformer architecture; section 5.4.7 identifies Llama Guard 3 as an 8B safety-classification fine-tune and distinguishes its tool-conversation screening from general tool generation. Does not define a separate active-parameter count for this classifier.

sources.title: Exact checkpoint config.json (gated)
sources.evidence: During the original October 26 audit, direct raw and rendered config requests returned HTTP 401. This historical access limitation is retained; the October 27 re-audit uses public cards, registry code and repository metadata without downloading weights or claiming a checkpoint-header census.

sources.title: Zipf’s and Heaps’ Laws for Tokens and LLM-generated Texts, Table 3
sources.publisher: Nikolay Mikhaylovskiy, NTR Labs / Tomsk State University; EMNLP Findings 2025
sources.evidence: Table 3 on PDF page 4 explicitly lists Llama-3.1-8B with Params 8B and Active params 8B. Section 4.1 uses the original base and instruction-finetuned models through Transformers in NF4 execution format; section 4.2 separately analyzes base-model outputs. This is the original researcher’s nominal active-count convention for the identified base model, not a Meta disclosure or direct Guard 3 measurement.

sources.title: Qwen3 Technical Report, Table 18
sources.evidence: Table 18 explicitly identifies LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct and reports Activated Params 8B and Total Params 8B. This independently corroborates the nominal convention for the instruction-tuned sibling; it is Qwen’s benchmark convention, not an exact Guard 3 count or the sole basis for transferring active size.

sources.title: Meta Llama Guard 3 8B INT8 model card
sources.evidence: The Usage section explicitly identifies this as the 8-bit version and links meta-llama/Llama-Guard-3-8B as the half-precision version. It describes bitsandbytes INT8 quantization, not output-vocabulary or layer pruning. The Llama 3 technical report likewise separates the quantized variant from the non-quantized classifier.

sources.title: Meta Llama Guard 3 model suite
sources.evidence: Explicitly calls Llama Guard 3-8B an 8B-parameter text classifier. Separately identifies the 1B model as including a quantized-and-pruned variant, and the 11B model as mixed-modality. This supports nominal 8B and prevents transferring the 1B pruning or vision changes to the standard 8B checkpoint.

name.note: Exact repository/SKU identifier; punctuation matches the frozen display name.

developer.note: Published by Meta in its model repository and release announcement.

family.note: Retains the broad Llama family; specifically the Llama Guard safety-classifier line, based on Llama 3.1 8B.

release_date.note: Dated first-party release announcement plus exact-variant documentation tying the 8B model to that Llama 3.1 release. The repository creation date is not used as public release evidence.

open_weights.note: Weights are distributed under gated license acceptance. Open weights does not imply an unrestricted license.

license.note: Exact Hugging Face checkpoint metadata and displayed agreement say Llama 3.1. Current PurpleLlama/8B/LICENSE instead says Llama 3.2; prefer the repository-specific weight terms and retain the conflict.

parameters_b.note: Derived full learned-parameter total, not checkpoint-header verified. s3 supplies h=4096, L=32, query heads=32, KV heads=8, vocab=128256, FFN multiplier=1.3 and rounding multiple=1024. s4 defines head_dim=h/32=128 and FFN width=1024*ceil(int(1.3*int(2*(4*h)/3))/1024)=14336. Formula: 2*128256*4096 + 32*(2*4096^2 + 2*4096*8*128 + 3*4096*14336 + 2*4096) + 4096 = 8,030,261,248. Includes untied input/output matrices and all norm weights; excludes KV caches, RoPE frequencies and quantization metadata. The exact BF16 repository storage total agrees independently; 8B remains the nominal size. October 27 re-audit retains this derivation after reopening the unchanged count-defining registry, reference output matrix and exact metadata; Meta’s suite README independently states nominal 8B. No new tensor census was performed.

active_parameters_b.note: Nominal 8B active count inferred through Meta’s explicit Llama-3.1-8B fine-tune relationship. Mikhaylovskiy’s original EMNLP 2025 Table 3 separately reports 8B active for that base model; Qwen3 Table 18 corroborates 8B for its Instruct sibling. The exact Guard registry preserves the base model’s count-defining dimensions and full 128256-token input/output vocabulary, with no added modality, experts or pruning identified for this checkpoint. The INT8 model is a separate quantized variant; the documented quantized-and-pruned model belongs to the 1B line. This transfers a published nominal research convention, not dense-equals-total arithmetic. Meta does not separately disclose Guard 3 active parameters or exact per-token tensor participation.

architecture.note: Dense decoder-only Transformer: 32 layers, width 4096, GQA with 32 query/8 KV heads, gated FFN and RMSNorm. Exact model registry and LlamaForCausalLM metadata support the classification; there is no expert router.

context_window.note: Meta registry explicitly selects 131072 for llama_guard_3_8b; corrects decimal shorthand 128000. This is the model sequence limit, not a claim about every provider endpoint.

modalities.note: 8B is explicitly text-only; generated outputs are safe/unsafe and hazard-category text. Vision support belongs to the separate 11B-Vision variant.

reasoning.note: The documented interface generates safety labels without a separately disclosed thinking mode; absence of that interface is not an explicit capability exclusion. Clear unsupported baseline false.

tool_call.note: The documented task screens conversations involving search/code-interpreter tools. Safety-label generation does not establish native tool-call generation or an absolute inability to do so; clear unsupported baseline false.

description.value: Llama 3.1 8B-based text safety classifier for prompts and responses in eight languages, covering 14 hazard categories including code interpreter abuse.
description.note: Concise description of the released classifier. The 14 labels comprise 13 MLCommons hazard categories plus Code Interpreter Abuse; no general assistant, reasoning-mode or tool-execution claim is transferred from Llama 3.1 Instruct.

patch.notes: 8.030261248B total is derived from Meta’s exact registry and reference weights, corroborated by BF16 repository metadata; nominal size is 8B. Nominal active 8B is inferred from the documented Llama 3.1 8B fine-tune lineage using Mikhaylovskiy’s Table 3 convention, corroborated for the Instruct sibling by Qwen3 Table 18. It is not a separate Meta active-count disclosure or exact per-token count. The standard checkpoint retains its full vocabulary; INT8 and pruned 1B variants are separate. Checkpoint headers were not accessed. The exact Hugging Face weights carry Llama 3.1 terms, while the current PurpleLlama 8B GitHub license copy says Llama 3.2. Tool-use support here means safety classification of tool conversations, not tool-call generation. Dedicated reasoning and native tool-call generation are not separately disclosed.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains the derived 8.030261248B total and Meta’s nominal 8B specification. Replaces the unresolved active count with a labeled nominal 8B lineage inference from the explicitly named Llama 3.1 8B base: Mikhaylovskiy’s original Table 3 reports 8B active, and Qwen3 Table 18 corroborates that convention for the Instruct sibling. Reopened Meta cards, model registry, reference implementation, repository metadata, model-suite README, technical report and INT8 documentation; the standard checkpoint preserves count-defining dimensions and full vocabulary. Fresh exact-name and pruning searches found no separate Meta Guard 3 active-count disclosure or structural change invalidating the inference. INT8 quantization is distinct; documented pruning applies to the 1B variant. Exact per-token participation remains unspecified. All twelve non-parameter field assessments are preserved.
